title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Note first that the neighbouring pages (numbered 160, 161) belong to a different text: Lipman's 'Rational singularities…', §25, on the E8 singularity u^2+v^3+w^5. They are interleaved in the archive and have nothing to do with this page. This page is a fragment of Grothendieck's 1965 'Galois theory of motives' notes.

Setting (reconstructed, partly conjectural):
- G is a motivic Galois group, or the automorphism group or gerbe of a fibre functor on a category of motives over Q.
- H is a normal subgroup with quotient G/H.
- xi in H^1(Q,H) is the class of a torsor, presumably the torsor of isomorphisms between two fibre functors or realizations.

The argument:
1. Localize at p. If eta_p in H^1(Q_p, G/H) is the class of a certain local torsor, then by 'general nonsense' the local component xi_p (the image of xi in H^1(Q_p,H)) equals partial(eta_p). Here partial is the coboundary of the exact sequence 1 -> H -> G -> G/H -> 1, in the non-abelian / twisted sense.
2. So xi_p is entirely determined by eta_p.
3. G/H is an extension 1 -> (G/H)^0 -> G/H -> Z^ -> 1 of the profinite constant group Z^ by its identity component. Grothendieck notes this extension splits and asserts H^1(Q_p, G/H) is isomorphic to H^1(Q_p, Z^) = Hom(pi_1(Q_p), Z^).
4. Hence eta_p is a homomorphism Gal(Q_p-bar/Q_p) -> Z^. To pin it down one uses the canonical isomorphism Gal(Q_p^nr/Q_p) = Z^ given by Frobenius.
5. Concretely, eta_p is the class of the torsor of isomorphisms between two fibre functors restricted to a subcategory written N_iv^0(M)^0, perhaps the 'niveau 0' (Artin–Tate type) part. The two functors are the base change (F_0)_{Q_p} of a rational fibre functor and a p-adic realization T_p. A parenthesis says the story works over any base field k, using T_p and a functor with values in W(k-bar)-modules. This is a Witt-vector, i.e. crystalline/Dieudonné-type, realization.
6. Finally a global statement. The components of xi along H^1(Q,H^0) and along H^1(Q,H_tr) (tr = toral/abelian part?) are determined by their local components at all places including infinity. For the last one, the reciprocity law sum_p inv_p = 0 means knowledge at the finite places suffices.

Purpose: compute the local (and hence global) invariants of the comparison torsor between fibre functors on motives over Q. The p-adic component is reduced to a Frobenius-normalized homomorphism to Z^, via a W(k-bar)-valued p-adic realization.
errors: The isomorphism H^1(Q_p,G/H) = H^1(Q_p,Z^) requires H^1(Q_p,(G/H)^0)=0 (and control of the twisted forms). Q_p is not of cohomological dimension 1, so this needs a hypothesis on (G/H)^0 (e.g. unipotent, or a torus with trivial H^1) that is not stated on the page.
'xi_p = partial(eta_p)' with eta_p in H^1 is not the standard abelian coboundary, which goes H^0(G/H) -> H^1(H) or H^1 -> H^2. It must be meant in a twisted/torsor sense, so it is loosely stated.

Using sum inv_p = 0 to recover the infinite place from the finite ones is valid only if that component behaves like a Brauer-type class with local invariants in Q/Z (e.g. via Tate–Nakayama for a torus). This is not justified here, and the margin note 'vérif' shows Grothendieck himself flagged it.

ideas.what: Local components of the global comparison torsor between fibre functors on motives over Q, analysed via the exact sequence H -> G -> G/H
ideas.modern_name: Torsors of isomorphisms between fibre functors in Tannakian categories; local-global analysis of motivic Galois gerbes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972), Deligne (1982, 'Motifs et groupes de Taniyama'; Tannakian categories 1990), Langlands–Rapoport (1987)
ideas.where_published: Ideas transmitted via Saavedra's thesis and Récoltes et Semailles mentions; not this computation

ideas.what: Quotient of the Galois group that is an extension of Z^ by a connected group, split by Frobenius at p
ideas.modern_name: Weil-group-like / Frobenius-split pseudomotivic Galois gerbe; Galois group of motives over finite fields

ideas.what: p-adic realization T_p with values in W(k-bar)-modules compared to the rational fibre functor over Q_p
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline realization / p-adic comparison fibre functor (Dieudonné-module, 'mysterious functor')
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's 1970 ICM talk discusses Dieudonné theory and the 'mysterious functor'; not this torsor computation

ideas.what: Using the reciprocity sum_p inv_p = 0 to deduce the component at infinity from the finite places

missed.claim: As early as 1965, Grothendieck computes the local components at p of the global torsor between fibre functors on motives over Q. He reduces them to a Frobenius-normalized class in Hom(pi_1(Q_p), Z^) via a torsor of isomorphisms with a W(k-bar)-valued p-adic realization. This anticipates the structure later formalized by Deligne (Taniyama group, local splittings at p) and by Langlands–Rapoport/Milne (Frobenius-split gerbes at p, crystalline fibre functors).
missed.quote: on travaille avec T_p sur ... fonct (W(k̄)) ... l'isom Gal(Q̃_p/Q_p) ≃ Ẑ donné par Frobenius
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is documentary evidence that the local-at-p analysis of motivic Galois gerbes, including a crystalline-type comparison torsor, was envisaged in Grothendieck's 1965 programme. That bears on the history of the Langlands–Rapoport conjecture and of p-adic Hodge theory. The fragment is too sketchy to constitute a new result, however.

missed.claim: A local-global description of the comparison class xi via its components in H^1(Q,H^0) and H^1(Q,H_tr), determined by local data, with the infinite place recovered by reciprocity. This is left marked 'vérif'.
missed.quote: les composantes de ξ suivant H¹(Q_p,H⁰) et H¹(Q_p,H_tr) sont connues quand on connaît leurs composantes en toutes places ... à cause de la formule Σ inv_p = 0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a Hasse-principle statement for motivic comparison torsors. Analogues appear in work on the Hasse principle for Taniyama/motivic gerbes (Milne, Langlands–Rapoport), but not in this form attributed to Grothendieck.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a sketchy fragment. It is of historical interest because it shows a 1965 local-at-p, Frobenius-normalized and W(k-bar)-crystalline analysis of motivic comparison torsors, prefiguring Deligne/Langlands–Rapoport. But the ideas are broadly known to have been in Grothendieck's motivic programme, and nothing here is a complete new result.
transcription_corrections: 'nonsense[?]' is plausibly 'non-sense' as in 'généralités non-sense' (general nonsense).
'si η_p ∂ est le suite exacte relative' should read roughly 'où ∂ est le cobord de la suite exacte relative'.
'On' before the exact sequence is likely 'Or'.
The exact sequence on the page is '→ (G/H)^0 → G/H → Ẑ →', with '(G/H)^0' written above; the parenthesis is '(extension qui se splitte)'.
'H_tr' is uncertain; it could be 'H_ab' or a toral part.
The final lines read: 'pour la dernière, à cause de la formule Σ inv_p = 0, il suffit de la connaître à distance finie', with 'vérif' in the left margin.
The neighbouring pages are from Lipman's rational singularities paper (§25, E8), interleaved in the archive and unrelated to this page.
